tagline: Dakar on its peninsula — island heritage hops, a colonial river city, and the Casamance corridor down the Atlantic coast.
summary: Senegal's marine-mobility heart is Dakar, a city on a peninsula reaching into the Atlantic, with the UNESCO heritage island of Gorée just offshore, the Madeleine islands national park, and the surf island of Ngor minutes away. Beyond the city, the coast runs north to the colonial river city of Saint-Louis and south, via a long Atlantic passage, to Ziguinchor in the Casamance. An existing Dakar–Gorée ferry proves the short-hop demand; the opportunity is a clean tier across the island hops and, on the Quanta-LR, the longer coastal corridors.
why_marine_mobility: Dakar's geography is a peninsula ringed by islands, and Senegal's coast is a string of river-and-sea cities. Navier's Pioneer II flies the island heritage hops — Dakar to Gorée, the Madeleine islands, Ngor — silent and zero-emission off the city's harbours, while the Quanta-LR's range opens the long Atlantic corridors to Saint-Louis and down to the Casamance that today rely on a single coastal ferry or slow road.

demand_signals.label: Gorée Island heritage ferry
demand_signals.note: The UNESCO World Heritage island of Gorée draws very heavy visitor and commuter traffic on the existing Dakar–Gorée ferry — proven short-hop water demand on a ~2.5 nm crossing.

demand_signals.label: Dakar peninsula & islands
demand_signals.note: Gorée, the Madeleine islands national park and Ngor surf island ring the Dakar peninsula, with the city itself spread along a coast where road traffic is heavy.

demand_signals.label: Casamance coastal corridor
demand_signals.note: Ziguinchor in the Casamance is linked to Dakar by a long Atlantic ferry passage or a slow road around The Gambia — a genuine line-haul corridor where water is competitive.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling tier on the Dakar–Gorée heritage crossing and the Madeleine and Ngor island hops, upgrading the existing ferry and slow leisure boats.
Cross-peninsula commuter hops between the Almadies, Yoff and Plateau waterfronts, bypassing Dakar's road congestion.
Long Atlantic coastal corridors to Saint-Louis (~90 nm) and the Casamance (Ziguinchor) on the Quanta-LR, where the hybrid range handles the open-coast distance.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Dakar island-and-peninsula mesh — Dakar Port↔Gorée (~2.5 nm), Dakar↔Madeleine islands (~2.2 nm), Ngor (~0.3 nm), Yoff↔Plateau (~8 nm) — sits far inside the 70 nm all-electric range on the sheltered peninsula waters off existing harbours.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long Atlantic corridors — Dakar↔Saint-Louis (~90 nm) and Dakar↔Ziguinchor (~200 nm) — are Quanta-LR hybrid routes (H2 2026+); the hybrid range and sea-keeping handle the open-coast distance and swell with no charging dependency, where an all-electric day-boat cannot reach.

signature_routes.label: Dakar Port ↔ Île de Gorée (all-electric heritage hop)
Dakar ↔ Madeleine Islands / Ngor (island leisure runs)

transit_planning: For the Port Autonome de Dakar, COSAMA (the Dakar–Ziguinchor ferry operator) or a tourism authority: a clean tier across the Dakar island hops and, with the Quanta-LR, the long Atlantic corridors that today rely on a single coastal ferry, off existing harbours.
competitive_landscape: Dakar has the established Gorée ferry and slow leisure boats to the islands; the Casamance corridor is served by a single state coastal ferry (COSAMA) or a slow road around The Gambia. There is no fast, clean, premium tier across the island hops or the coastal corridors.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the Senegalese maritime administration (ANAM) and the Port Autonome de Dakar, with the Madeleine islands a national park favouring low-wash, zero-emission craft. Senegal's tourism and coastal-development priorities support a clean water-transport tier, and the heritage status of Gorée aligns with a quiet, low-impact platform.
seasonality: The Dakar peninsula waters are navigable year-round in a warm, dry climate, with the Atlantic swell heaviest in the winter months; the island hops run consistently, while the long coastal corridors favour the calmer season. Tourism peaks in the cooler, drier November–May window.
